newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CIM, RJB in new share agreement.
newsitem.headline: CIM, RJB in new share agreement.

text.p: Australian coal miner CIM Resources Ltd said on Sunday it extended the term of the existing subscription agreement with British coal miner RJB Mining Plc by 18 months.
CIM said under the new agreement RJB would have the right to subscribe A$113.6 million for a further 110 million shares until December 1998.

Under the existing agreement, RJB subscribed A$22.5 million for 25 million shares or 12.5 percent of CIM's issued capital. RJB also has the right to subscribe for additional tranches of shares, which would increase its stake to 43 percent.
CIM said the deal is subject to approval by the Foreign Investment Review Board.

"The second subscription agreement arises from the commitment of both CIM and RJB to preserve the existing arrangements between the companies and to ensure adequate funding is available for the continuing growth of CIM," it said.

It said the deal provides a closer alignment of the interests of RJB and CIM, as such RJB will not take any other direct interests in the Australian coal industry during the extended term of the agreement.

"RJB will further support CIM by providing funding of up to A$50 million for the construction of the Duralie project, once all statutory approvals and formal board approval is in place for the development of the project," CIM said.
The Duralie coal project is based in New South Wales.
RJB first bought into CIM last May, when CIM made a placement of 25 million shares at 90 cents each.
CIM shares closed one cent lower at 67 cents on Friday.
